claims.claim: Fifty Homilies transmitted under Macarius the Egyptian (c. 300–391) but now ascribed to an anonymous Syrian monk of the late 4th c., sometimes identified with Symeon of Mesopotamia.
Macarius the Egyptian, also known as Macarius the Elder, was a Coptic monk, hermit and priest born around AD 300 who died in the Scetis desert about AD 391.
He was a prominent Desert Father who founded a semi‑eremitic monastic community at Scetis and was renowned for his ascetic practice, prophetic gifts and spiritual instruction.
The authorship of the fifty homilies is disputed; scholars label them “Pseudo‑Macarius” because it cannot be proved that Macarius himself composed them in their final form.
The Spiritual Homilies are regarded as a classic of early Christian mystical theology and have been highly influential in the spiritual formation of Eastern monasticism.
